headline: Cut LinkedIn 33% ($300 to $200/day) because every model shows it is the costliest channel at about $139 CPA, and test Google search incrementality before moving its budget.

moves.reason: Cut 33%. CPA $138.92 last 7d (4wk avg $138.41), ROAS 1.13 vs 1.35; 13-week CPA never below $97. All five models agree it is the costliest channel (implied CPA $79-$141 vs $43-$58 Meta), spread only 4 pts, so cut is not dependent on one model's rule. Cheap to reverse.

tests.hypothesis: Google search's true incremental share is well below the 66.8% last-touch credit (first-touch 32.3%); a meaningful part of its conversions are captured demand from buyers persuaded by email/Meta/word of mouth.
tests.design: Geo-split holdout: pick matched regions, cut Google search (especially brand terms) by ~50% in the treatment half for 4 weeks while holding the rest constant. Measure total conversions and revenue across all channels incl. direct in both halves, plus self-reported 'Google' share. Compare total-conversion drop to the ~185 weekly search conversions reported. Pre-register a stop rule if total conversions drop >15%.

flag_verdicts.reason: Google spend spiked 2026-09-12 to 09-18 (1.77x median). Conversions rose too: 271 in week of 09-14 vs 187 the week before, and CPA was $23.90 vs $28.54. Spend has since returned to about $4.1k/week and the last week's CPA is $19.94. No lasting efficiency loss.

Direct rose from 0.5 to 0.7 per day with flat paid spend, but the counts are tiny (2-8 per week, only 2 last week, below the prior 4-week average of 6.25). The AI-answer share went 2% to 5% on roughly 100 responses a week, and it fell back to 1% in the latest week. This is too noisy to credit any paid channel, or to act on. Re-check next run.

flags.message: google_search spend jumped for 7 days (2026-09-12 to 2026-09-18); CPA held at $26 vs $23. Likely fine, confirm before acting.
Direct conversions grew 1.5x (0.5 to 0.7/day) while paid spend moved 1.00x. Self-reported AI answers went from 2% to 5%. Something untracked is driving buyers.
